set.body:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 0 item 4.

The README implies distortion detection, fidelity facets and intrusion mass as validated capabilities (no efficacy evidence; the mode gate never refused anything on Sherlock), says grakern is unpublished (the build clones the pinned commit), gets the module count wrong, and says the encoder was never compared with lexical baselines (it was: study-log:181). tools/recall-study/README.md:35-37 calls agreement the primary outcome; a comment at RecallToVideo.scala:545-557 carries the same framing.

Scope:
Text and comment corrections only; no behaviour change.

Acceptance criteria:
1. README states distortion/facet/intrusion outputs have no efficacy evidence, with a pointer to the evidence status.
2. README's grakern note matches build.sbt; its module count matches build.sbt (16 cross-platform + 8 JVM-only as of 2026-09-18).
3. README's statement about lexical baselines is corrected with a citation.
4. tools/recall-study/README.md and the RecallToVideo.scala comment no longer call agreement the primary outcome or judge of record.
5. The commit body lists grep commands showing the retired phrases are gone.
6. `sbt -batch embedBench/compile scalafmtCheckAll` passes (a Scala comment changed) and `cd docs-site && npm run verify:examples` passes.

Gate: fresh-context cold review of the committed text; the commit body states what changed and
what it does not establish.

Size: S.
set.title: Phase 0: correct false and overstated claims in README and the recall-study docs
